turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning. Your daughter's brought you in about these turns. Dizzy, is that right?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, yes, a bit, when I stand up. But I haven't fallen, doctor, I just sort of slid. I'm worried it's something awful. Is it a stroke?
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Mum, you went down twice. Once by the kettle and once getting off the loo. I had to lift you. That's not sliding.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): It wasn't a proper fall though. My legs just went a bit soft. I didn't black out or anything.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Twice. When?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, the first was... I think Thursday? Or was it the week before. I can't pin it down. Sorry.
[SEG0007] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thursday last week, and the Monday before that. So just under a fortnight.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): Dizzy only on standing?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, I get up from the settee and the room goes swimmy, and it frightens me. Sitting I'm alright. How long does that sort of thing last, normally?
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Seconds or minutes?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): A few seconds, then it eases if I hold the chair. Sometimes a minute. I don't know exactly.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no pain. Should I be worried about my heart though? My neighbour had a heart attack and she was dizzy.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): No shortness of breath?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No, breathing's fine. I am tired though, ever so washed out this last fortnight.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Headache? Weakness in one arm?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No headache, and my arms are alright, both of them. Why, do you think it's a stroke? Please just tell me.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not from what you've said. Tablets. Blood pressure and a sleeping tablet, yes?

[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, amlodipine, that's ten milligrams in the morning, and the other blood pressure one, ramipril, and zopiclone at night. I do take them. Do I have to stop them all? I won't sleep.

[SEG0020] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ramipril is five milligrams. Zopiclone is seven point five. She takes the zopiclone every night, doctor, has done for years. The amlodipine she sometimes misses if she's rushing.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't miss them. Well, maybe once or twice. Not really.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): So amlodipine ten milligrams most mornings, ramipril five, zopiclone seven point five at night. Any allergies?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing I'm allergic to. Is the zopiclone the problem? I read they make old people fall.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Possibly. I'll stop the zopiclone and leave the blood pressure tablets as they are.

[SEG0025] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She's been on that sleeping tablet since Dad died, about five-ish years. If you stop it she'll be up all night. The dizziness is in the morning, after she's stood up, not in the night.

[SEG0026] person_4 (NURSE): Sorry to butt in. Lying blood pressure a hundred and fifty-two over eighty-six, pulse seventy-four. Standing, after a minute, a hundred and ten over sixty-eight, pulse ninety-six.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. That drop changes things. Forget stopping the zopiclone. We'll stop the amlodipine instead and keep the ramipril and the sleeping tablet for now.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Stop the amlodipine completely? Not just a smaller dose? What if my blood pressure shoots up? And can I still take the zopiclone tonight?
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes, stop amlodipine from today. Ramipril five milligrams stays. Zopiclone seven point five you can take tonight. We'll recheck the pressure.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Will I feel worse before I feel better? I'm really anxious about falling again, even if I say I only slid.
[SEG0031] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She slid because her legs went. She was on the floor both times. I think you should know that properly.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Noted. No blackout, you said. Any palpitations?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): No, it doesn't race. I just feel panicky sitting here, that's all. Is ninety-six too fast?
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): That pulse was on standing. It's acceptable. Drink plenty, stand up slowly, and sit if it swims. Don't drive until this settles.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't drive. Should I get a frame? And what about the chemist, do I just not collect the amlodipine?
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Don't collect it. No frame today. We'll sort a review on the way out.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): What if I go down again tomorrow? Do I ring you or nine nine nine? I need to know which.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): If you black out, injure yourself, or can't get up, it's nine nine nine. Otherwise ring the surgery the next morning.
[SEG0039] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll stay with her tonight. She lives alone usually, but I'm there till Sunday.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): You don't have to fuss. I'm fine, honestly, mostly. Will stopping one tablet really fix the swimming feeling?
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): It's the most likely culprit, given that standing drop. Not definite until we recheck. Any questions left that aren't repeats?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Just... if the ramipril is five milligrams, is that a lot? I get muddled with the numbers.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): It's a standard dose. Keep taking it. Reception will book you back in one week.

symptoms.name: dizziness on standing
symptoms.frequency: on standing, lasting a few seconds to a minute

social_history.description: Lives alone usually, with her daughter staying until Sunday

physical_examination.finding: blood pressure drop on standing after one minute, with pulse rise

clinical_assessment.assessment: The dizzy swimming feeling is most likely caused by amlodipine, given the standing blood pressure drop

clinical_actions.description: Stop amlodipine from today
Initial plan to stop zopiclone and leave both blood pressure tablets was reversed after the standing blood pressure drop; continue zopiclone for now and stop amlodipine instead
Continue ramipril 5 mg and zopiclone 7.5 mg at night
Recheck blood pressure
Drink plenty, stand up slowly, sit if it swims, and do not drive until this settles
Do not collect amlodipine from the chemist
Call 999 if she blacks out, is injured, or cannot get up; otherwise ring the surgery the next morning
Follow-up consultation

clinical_uncertainties.description: The patient says she only slid and did not really fall, while her daughter reports two falls to the floor.
The patient could not date the first episode, and her daughter then said the Monday before last Thursday and Thursday last week.
The daughter says amlodipine is sometimes missed, and the patient then said maybe once or twice.

contradictions_detected: Patient maintains she slid rather than fell, while her daughter reports two falls to the floor.

spec.situation: Older patient who fell twice 'but not really fell, slid down'; dizzy on standing; takes several BP and sleeping tablets; daughter reports what the patient minimises; nurse reads lying and standing BP; doctor changes one tablet.
features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.

spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.

bad.reason: Dose, indication, current use supported; current status also confirmed by doctor, not only family member.
bad.text: ramipril (dose=5 mg, indication=blood pressure, status=currently_used, reported_by=family_member)

bad.reason: All advice supported except 'sit if dizzy'; transcript says sit if it swims.
bad.text: Drink plenty, stand up slowly, sit if dizzy, and do not drive until it settles (action_type=counselling, status=recommended, responsible_person=patient)

omissions.text: Orthostatic hypotension was demonstrated by lying-to-standing observations: blood pressure fell from 152/86 lying to 110/68 after 1 minute standing, with pulse rising from 74 to 96; this drop 'changes things' and prompted the doctor to revise the plan.

The doctor initially said he would stop zopiclone and leave the blood pressure tablets unchanged, but then reversed this after the standing blood pressure results and decided to continue zopiclone for now and stop amlodipine instead.
Negative finding asked and answered: no weakness in either arm / both arms are alright (not just one arm).
